title: Define inference SLA/SLOs and gradual rollout constraints for Runtime 2.0
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Summary: Define concrete SLA / SLO targets, SLIs, error budgets, and rollout gates for the Runtime 2.0 upgrade so that engineering, SRE, and PM have a single source of truth for release gating. This ticket captures requirements, clarifications, scope adjustments, and acceptance criteria.

Context: Runtime 2.0 contains several performance improvements (kernel selection changes, batching heuristics, KV caching) and a new autoscaling policy. We must avoid regressions for latency-sensitive customers and provide clear rollback criteria. The initial PRD focused on p95 latency targets; stakeholders requested uptime SLOs and explicit error budget rules to govern rollouts.

Scope: "Define and document": (1) SLO targets by API surface (text generation, chat streaming, embeddings), (2) SLIs and measurement methodology (synthetic vs production sampling), (3) error budget math and burn rate alert thresholds, (4) deterministic rollout gates and traffic ramp schedule, (5) dashboards and runbook links, (6) automated rollback triggers. Not in scope: implementation of new metric collectors (covered in ENG-2890), or changes to billing logic.

Trade-offs and clarifications: We will reuse the existing metrics pipeline (Datadog + internal metrics aggregator) for SLI calculation to avoid instrumenting new collectors. For very low-volume customers we will rely on synthetic canaries for latency measurements. The SLOs are intentionally conservative for the first 30 days of rollouts to prioritize stability over small latency wins.

Open questions (to resolve in PRD review): Which embeddings request size buckets should map to which latency SLOs? Do enterprise customers with dedicated capacity get separate SLOs? (Tentative answer: yes, dedicated contracts can negotiate different SLOs; record in release notes.)
acceptance_criteria: SLOs documented and approved by SRE and Product: p95 and p99 latency targets for text-generation, streaming-chat, and embeddings; uptime objective defined for hosted API
SLIs defined with measurement windows and sources: synthetic canary (1min), production sampled SLIs (5min rolling), and post-rollout 24h aggregated metrics
Error budget math documented: monthly error budget computed from uptime SLO; example calculations for 99.95% and 99.9%
Alerting rules created in Datadog for burn-rate and absolute threshold breaches, with runbook references
Rollout gates enumerated and automated where possible (canary check, quality regressions, burn-rate check), and gating automation tested in staging
Traffic ramp schedule captured with hard guardrails and automatic rollback on gate failures
Dashboards created: SLO status, burn-rate, latency distributions, request volume by model/region
Runbook and incident playbook added to Confluence with rollback commands and owners
Executive sign-off from SRE and Product on the SLO document and rollout plan
success_metrics: No more than 1% of rollouts require emergency rollback after first 30 days
Measured p95 latency stays within defined SLOs for 95% of customer traffic during rollouts
Error budget burn rate alerts triggered < 3 times per quarter for major releases
Runbook used successfully in at least one simulated rollback drill before GA
rollout_gates: Gate 1 - Canary health (automated): Deploy to canary fleet (5% traffic or 1000 rps cap) for 2 hours. Gate passes if: p95 latency regression <= +10% relative to baseline AND error rate delta <= +0.02%.
Gate 2 - Synthetic stability: 30-minute synthetic canary run across 3 regions; passes if latency SLI within target and no functional errors
Gate 3 - Burn-rate check: During canary, 1h burn-rate < 1.5. If burn-rate >= 2 for 30m, automatically pause rollout and page SRE
Gate 4 - Quality regression detection: Prompt set evals (pre-registered) show no regression beyond defined thresholds; must pass automated evals in CI

Gate 5 - Gradual ramp policy: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with minimum observation windows [1h, 2h, 4h, 12h, 24h] respectively. Any gate failure triggers immediate rollback to previous stable version
Gate 6 - Post-ramp observation: 72h monitoring window after 100% with final SLOs validated before removing soft limits

We agreed to use rolling windows of 30d for monthly error budget calculations and 7d windows for intermediate sanity checks.
Dedicated customers can opt into contract-level SLOs; default public hosted API SLOs documented above.
